subject: Website tracking review & evidence for DPA - pixels, cookies, consent
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@solsticemedia.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Solstice Media Legal <privacy@solsticemedia.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Feb 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Website tracking and cookie policy — GDPR / evidence request

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this on. We're going through our DPA and SIG review for a customer procurement gate and need a short audit of the trackers/pixels on our marketing site (solsticemedia.com). Specifically:

- A breakdown of third-party pixels currently firing (vendor, purpose, data types collected).
- Whether the pixel is configurable to operate on consent-only gating (CMP-compatible).
- Any PII or identifiers that could be passed (email hash, device identifiers).
- A copy or pointer to your cookie policy text and confirmation of lawful basis (consent/legitimate interest).

Procurement has asked for the above plus an initial DPIA (if you think a DPIA is needed). Is there someone on your side who can review the pixel list and confirm whether you can provide a short evidence pack (screenshots, policy excerpt, vendor contracts) we can attach to the SIG/CAIQ?

We're on a tight timeline — would appreciate an ETA by EOD Monday.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Solstice Media

(Attachment requested: none in this initial email)

Date: Fri, 14 Feb 2025 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Website tracking and cookie policy — GDPR / evidence request

Hi Elena — thanks for the detail. I'll coordinate this from Legal and loop in Security and Product.

Quick plan:
1) Vivek will run an initial scan of solsticemedia.com and produce a pixel inventory (vendor, endpoint, data types).
2) Product will confirm whether any pixel data flows to model training or other downstream systems (we'll isolate those).
3) I'll draft the evidence pack (policy excerpt, screenshots, vendor contract excerpts) and let you know if we need a DPIA.

Can you upload any existing inventory or the draft cookie policy if you have it? That will accelerate things.

ETA: initial inventory by Mon 17 Feb EOD; full evidence pack + DPIA recommendation by Thu 20 Feb.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

(Please note: internal participants only from Redwood team)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Feb 2025 10:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Website tracking and cookie policy — GDPR / evidence request

Neha / Marissa — ran an automated scan (DevTools + crawler) and a light passive capture. High level:

- Found ~8 third-party endpoints firing across marketing pages: Google Analytics (analytics.js), Meta Pixel (connect.facebook.net), LinkedIn Insight Tag, Hotjar, Segment, a TikTok pixel, and two marketing vendor pixels (adx.tracker.vendorx.net and px.conv.vendory.com).
- Data observed: standard UA client IDs, page URLs, referrer, and in some cases hashed email digests where a form appears prefilled & hashed on submit (we did not receive raw emails in the request).
- Consent gating: GA and some Segment snippets are configurable; Meta Pixel and one vendor pixel are currently firing before consent on the global header (we saw snippets inserted above consent check in production).

Attached: pixel_inventory.csv (columns: page, vendor, endpoint, fires_before_consent, data_sent_summary).

Immediate recommendations:
- Move all marketing pixels behind CMP-triggered callbacks.
- Remove any client-side hashing of emails before you have explicit user consent (or switch to server-side consent-validated flows).
- Take a closer look at Hotjar recordings — might capture PII if forms are present.

I'll need dev access or a staging URL for a follow-up to confirm fix implementation.

Attaching: pixel_inventory.csv (stub).

Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: pixel_inventory.csv)

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@solsticemedia.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Solstice Media Legal <privacy@solsticemedia.com>, OneTrust Support <support@onetrust.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Feb 2025 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Website tracking and cookie policy — GDPR / evidence request

Thanks Vivek — this is exactly the kind of detail procurement needs. I've attached our working inventory and a draft cookie policy (solstice_cookie_policy_draft.pdf).

Notes:
- The hashed email appears to be sent by our newsletter widget before the CMP callback — we're escalating to marketing to confirm.
- Procurement specifically requested: (a) confirmation we can provide vendor subprocessor clauses/SCCs for any vendor sending PII, (b) a brief statement on whether Redwood uses any tracking that would be considered profiling under GDPR, and (c) a suggested DPIA scope if needed.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood produces any profiling outputs from marketing pixels (i.e., does any captured identifier feed into personalization models?) and whether you can provide copies of SCC/addenda for the listed vendors?

Elena

(Attachments: pixel_inventory.csv, solstice_cookie_policy_draft.pdf)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@solsticemedia.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Feb 2025 16:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Website tracking and cookie policy — GDPR / evidence request

Elena — thanks for the inventory and draft policy. Quick summary and next steps from Redwood:

1) Profiling / model training: we do not feed marketing pixel telemetry into our product model training pipelines. Analytics and attribution events are separated and retained per our retention policy; anything that could be considered behavioral profiling is handled by our marketing stack (we do not use marketing pixel signals for ML personalization). We'll provide a short attestation for procurement.

2) SCCs / vendor contracts: for common vendors (Google, Meta, LinkedIn, Hotjar, Segment) we can provide standard DPA/SCC addenda. For smaller vendors (vendorx, vendory) we'll surface contract status and whether SCCs are in place.

3) DPIA recommendation: given the mix of third-party recorders and hashed identifiers, I recommend a scoped DPIA focused on "marketing/tracking data flows". Vivek will provide the scoped DPIA template items; I've attached a DPIA_template.docx for your use.

4) Timeline & asks for you: please provide a staging URL (or dev credentials) so our engineers can validate fixes behind consent gates. Also confirm whether you want a redlined cookie policy back or a short policy excerpt we can include in the evidence pack.

Deliverables and ETA:
- Attestation on profiling: Mon 24 Feb
- Vendor SCCs/DPA excerpts: Tue 25 Feb (initial set)
- Scoped DPIA draft + evidence pack (policy excerpt, screenshots): Thu 27 Feb

Links: https://hub.redwood.ai/hubspot/records/HS-9812 (procurement ticket).

Attaching: DPIA_template.docx

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: DPIA_template.docx)
